challenges.title: Bike builder site
challenges.brief: We need a small website for Tidewater Bikes, a frame builder that makes steel city bikes to order in Michigan. It is for riders weighing up a bike of their own: they should understand what makes us different, meet the people who build the frames and see what each model costs. A visitor must be able to reach every page from every other page, and no link may lead nowhere. Build it cleanly, with one shared stylesheet and nothing heavy. All the wording is supplied, so put your effort into how it is put together. The attached reference site is the exact target; match it as closely as you can, page for page. Done means a rider can get from the home page to a price in one click.
acceptance: From any page I can reach every other page in one click
No link leads to a missing page
Every page shares one look and one stylesheet
The three models and their prices are easy to compare
It matches the reference site closely, page for page

challenges.title: Restaurant site
challenges.brief: Olive & Ember, our wood-fired restaurant on the harbour, needs a proper website. It is for people deciding where to eat: they want a feel for the place, a look at the menu with prices, a way to request a table, and to know where we are and when we are open. Every page must be reachable from every other page, the booking link must always be close at hand, and nothing may lead nowhere. Build it cleanly on one shared stylesheet, keep it light, and make sure the booking form works for everyone, including keyboard and screen reader users. The wording is supplied. The attached reference site is the exact target; match it as closely as you can. Done means a guest can go from the home page to a booking request in two clicks.

requirements.text: Five pages exist in one folder: index.html (the home page), catalogue.html, product.html, basket.html and contact.html
Every page has the site name leading home and the menu Home, Catalogue, Basket, Contact, in that order, leading to the matching pages
Every footer links Home, Catalogue, Featured tea (product.html), Basket and Contact, then '© 2026 Kettle & Leaf · 14 Mill Lane, Bristol'
The home page has the heading, intro, a 'Shop the catalogue' button leading to catalogue.html and six favourite teas with pictures and prices, each a link
The catalogue page has a filter form (Type tick boxes, Price choice, Apply filters) and all twelve teas with prices in the reference order, each leading to product.html
The product page shows Darjeeling First Flush, £9.80, its description, a Size choice, a Quantity field, 'Add to basket' and three related teas
The basket page has a table with header cells (Tea, Size, Qty, Price), three lines, Subtotal £39.20, Delivery £3.50 and Total £42.70, then a checkout form ending in Place order
The contact page has a form (Your name, Email, Message, Send message), the shop address, an email link and an opening-hours table
Every form field has a label, and email fields use the email input type
All styling lives in shop.css and forms.css, shared by every page; no style blocks or style attributes
Every page has its own title, lang="en", header, nav, main and footer landmarks, and text alternatives on its pictures
Calm and natural: white header, deep green banner and footer, amber buttons and current-page underline, serif headings

challenges.title: Documentation site
challenges.brief: Lumen is our small static site generator, and its documentation needs a home. It is for developers who have just heard of Lumen: they should be able to install it, set it up, put a site online, look up any option and see what changed in each release. A reader must be able to reach every page from every other page, always know where they are, and move through the guide in order without hunting. No link may lead nowhere, including links between folders. Build it cleanly on one shared stylesheet and keep it light. The wording, code samples and tables are supplied. The attached reference site is the exact target; match it as closely as you can, page for page. Done means a newcomer can go from the overview to a deployed site by following the pages.

challenges.title: Portfolio and blog
challenges.brief: I'm Mara Quinn, an independent designer and front-end developer, and I need a portfolio site with a blog. It is for the charities, councils and studios who might hire me: they should see what I do and have done, read my writing, learn a little about me and get in touch easily. Every page must be reachable, readers must be able to move between posts and back to the blog, and no link may lead nowhere, even from posts kept in folders two levels down. Build it cleanly on one shared stylesheet and keep it quick on a slow connection. The wording is supplied. The attached reference site is the exact target; match it as closely as you can, page for page. Done means a visitor can go from any post to my contact form in one click.

challenges.title: Conference site
challenges.brief: We are running Fieldwork 2027, a one-day conference on field research, and it needs a website. It is for researchers deciding whether to come: they should see the day's programme, find out who is speaking and what each talk is about, reserve tickets and get answers to the usual questions. Every page must be reachable, every speaker must have a page of their own, reachable wherever that speaker is named, and no link may lead nowhere, including from the speaker pages. Build it cleanly on one shared stylesheet, keep it light, and make the ticket form work for everyone. The wording is supplied. The attached reference site is the exact target; match it as closely as you can, page for page. Done means a visitor can go from a talk on the schedule to its speaker and back.
acceptance: From the home page I can reach every page in at most two clicks
No link leads to a missing page, including from the speaker pages
Wherever a speaker is named in a list or the schedule, I can open their page
Every field on the ticket form is clearly labelled and works with a keyboard
Every page shares one look and one stylesheet
It matches the reference site closely, page for page
